scope: Static x86 disassembly and direct-reference audit. Isolated lease helper only; no live combat integration, compilation, unit execution, native emulation or full-game execution in this investigation.
acquisition: 10383fa0 has a single slot (10383fe0 cmp esi,1). An index FFFF, mismatching handle-table generation, null current object pointer, or equal full requester handle reaches the available branch. A valid different handle returns false.

At 10383ff4/10383ffb only requestedSeconds > 0 writes BOTH owner and duration. A check using -1 returns availability with no writes, even when the old handle is stale. The requester handle itself is not separately validated in this function.

10384040 selects float 0.5 for Request=true and -1 for Request=false. Same-owner positive requests overwrite duration, rather than taking its maximum; a 0.5-second request can shorten an existing 2-second refresh.

Refresh action start callback 101e44a0 requests 2 seconds and returns the acquisition result. Update callback 101e7a20 returns false only if action+0x1c is null; otherwise it requests 2 seconds using owner action+0x28 and unconditionally returns AL=1, even if the manager denied acquisition.
expiry: 10382ee0 tail 1038321d..10383248: read remaining; skip if remaining<0; subtract incoming float dt; store; invalidate owner only if resulting remaining<0. Exact zero keeps ownership until a later positive dt. Clearing writes FFFF at +0x504 and zero at +0x506; negative remaining is retained.

Caller 10360a40 compares root+0 with root+4 to avoid duplicate work in one epoch. It obtains clock data through 10823430, uses float at returned object+0x30, skips zero dt, stamps root+4, then calls manager update at 10360ab5. The timer is not decremented per aircraft.

No immediate action-exit release is established: Refresh action slot6 is 101e7a60 (ret only). Its destructor 101e79f0 -> 101e4d10 detaches action state without a manager/token call. Direct +0x504/+0x508 accesses in this manager family resolve to construction, acquisition and expiry; this bounded audit does not prove absence of arbitrary indirect memory writes.
lifetime: 10364d20 allocates one 0x1060-byte root, invokes 10364980 and stores its pointer in global 11263a00. Root constructor allocates the 0x1a28 manager, constructs it via 103854e0 at 10364a09, and stores it at root+0x1c at 10364a17.
Manager constructor initializes the owner through 107dad20 (FFFF index, zero generation) at 103855af and remaining=-1 at 103855bc.
10364d90 destroys/frees the root and nulls the global. Root destructor 10364b90 calls manager cleanup 10385750 at 10364c43, frees it, and nulls root+0x1c at 10364c56.

Root creation is called by 104e50b0 at 104e51be; that surrounding routine contains Level, LOADINGSPLASH, startup assets and InGame Simulation Task setup. Teardown 104e5c90 calls root destruction at 104e62c4. Active-level/session scope is inferred from this surrounding load/teardown code; the global pointer and lack of target/team/aircraft keys are direct evidence.

minecraftAdaptation: One helper instance per ServerLevel, supplied by a future coordinator; no process-global static owner and no per-target/per-team token. This world partition is explicitly an MC adaptation, not evidence of native multiple dimensions.

UUID plus a same-world present/not-removed entity lookup substitutes for native index+generation+nonnull-pointer validity. Do not equate validity with current target, current attack action or health>0. Lookup must not force chunk loading.

Advance once per world simulation step using a float duration. Do not convert the source strict-negative boundary into an unconditional <=0 tick deadline; floating subtraction can affect exact-zero timing.

No release API is introduced. Stopping refresh leaves the token to expire naturally; entity invalidation permits another positive request; world unload discards the coordinator. Null arguments and nonfinite/negative dt are rejected as MC boundary constraints.
The helper refresh method returns actual acquisition success. Integrating the original action lifecycle must separately preserve the start-callback vs update-callback return-value difference.
